input.old_string:
I am a PhD researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in GeoAI, remote sensing, and AI-driven hydrological modelling. My research focuses on designing deep learning frameworks that estimate snow hydrology parameters — specifically snow cover fraction (SCF) and snow water equivalent (SWE) — from multi-sensor Earth observation data, contributing to climate-resilient water resource management.

A central thread of my work is multi-sensor data fusion: merging Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, DEM, and reanalysis data streams to overcome the limitations of any single sensor and improve accuracy in complex Alpine and Arctic environments. These estimates are critical inputs for hydrological modelling and for quantifying the impacts of climate change on snowmelt-driven river systems.

My academic background spans Ethiopia, France, Spain, Hungary, Finland, and Sweden — from a BSc and MSc at Bahir Dar University, through an Erasmus Mundus Joint MSc in Image Processing & Computer Vision, to research secondments at RISE Sweden and University of Florida TREC. I am co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop (Sep 2026, Tampere, Finland) and actively contribute to the GeoAI community through publications, conference presentations, and open-source tools.
input.new_string:
I am a PhD researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, working at the intersection of Geospatial AI, remote sensing, and computer vision. My research develops deep learning and multimodal fusion frameworks that extract environmental intelligence from multi-sensor Earth observation data — combining SAR, optical, multispectral, and auxiliary data sources to monitor and model our changing planet.

I work across the full EO pipeline: from multi-sensor and multimodal data fusion (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2, DEM, reanalysis) to computer vision architectures for semantic segmentation and scene understanding, through to adapting geospatial foundation models for downstream environmental tasks. Applications span hydrology, land cover mapping, environmental change detection, and climate impact assessment.

My academic path spans six countries — BSc and MSc at Bahir Dar University (Ethiopia), an Erasmus Mundus Joint MSc in Image Processing & Computer Vision across France, Spain, and Hungary, and research secondments at RISE Sweden and University of Florida TREC. I am co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 (Tampere, Finland) and contribute actively to the GeoAI community through publications, open-source tools, and conference presentations.

About Me

Doctoral researcher at the intersection of Geospatial AI, remote sensing, and computer vision — building intelligent systems that decode the Earth from space.

20 Citations
5 Publications
4 Years Research
6 Projects

I am a PhD researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, working at the intersection of Geospatial AI, remote sensing, and computer vision. My research develops deep learning and multimodal fusion frameworks that extract environmental intelligence from multi-sensor Earth observation data — combining SAR, optical, multispectral, and auxiliary data sources to monitor and model our changing planet.

I work across the full EO pipeline: from multi-sensor and multimodal data fusion (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2, DEM, reanalysis) to computer vision architectures for semantic segmentation and scene understanding, through to adapting geospatial foundation models for downstream environmental tasks. Applications span hydrology, land cover mapping, environmental change detection, and climate impact assessment.

My academic path spans six countries — BSc and MSc at Bahir Dar University (Ethiopia), an Erasmus Mundus Joint MSc in Image Processing & Computer Vision across France, Spain, and Hungary, and research secondments at RISE Sweden and University of Florida TREC. I am co-organising the HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026 (Tampere, Finland) and contribute actively to the GeoAI community through publications, open-source tools, and conference presentations.
